decisions.rationale: Exhaustive review found no comparator with the same GitHub projection-gate authority, boundary, outcome, and race semantics. The listed features address freshness, precedence, generic mutation TOCTOU, or dispatch blocking and remain adjacent owner or consumer contracts.

No comparator jointly owns the GitHub mutation prerequisite snapshot, dispatch binding, remote idempotency, and reconciliation failure boundary. Generic approval and mutation race controls are related but distinct.

The anchor requires a GitHub attribution envelope and caller-to-consumer propagation seam. Comparator features cover container identity, generic provider identity, joins, or runtime-context visibility, so shared cross-surface vocabulary does not make them merge-equivalent.

No comparator has the same GitHub usage-and-audit identity record lifecycle, credential tombstoning, account deletion, and support-export boundary. The listed privacy lifecycles govern different record families or routing seams.

No comparator matches the confirmed GitHub browser-auth mutation handoff, provenance, cancellation, rollback, and recovery transaction. Other login, OAuth, setup, and blocked-recovery contracts use different providers or state boundaries.
The similarly worded retirement records govern distinct PlanUnits and product authorities. Their common migration-lineage pattern is adjacency, not the same retired bridge feature.

The Git remote-only adapter disconnect and in-flight resynchronization lifecycle is not duplicated. Generic adapter bounds, host blockers, provider-stream failures, container reconciliation, and blocked recovery are neighboring contracts with different authorities and outcomes.

Browser/device polling appears elsewhere, but it belongs to DockerHub and differs in provider authority and terminal recovery state. Generic provider and readiness recovery features are also distinct.

The anchor combines account-root isolation, provider import, sharing boundaries, and cooldown revalidation. Comparator features cover profile isolation, auth selection, switching, or packet binding as members or consumers, not the same full feature.

Authentication setup, API-key registration, device polling, removal compensation, and removal data lifecycle form one Multi-Account feature. The listed auth, OAuth, refresh, privacy, and recovery features are narrower or provider-specific neighbors.

No comparator shares the credential-route epoch authority together with native token-store atomicity and rotating-fetch failover. Credential refresh, custody, cache, and auth-state features are members or dependencies with distinct boundaries.

This anchor is an umbrella over permission matching, approval recovery, assistance authority, metadata, UI, and secret scope. All plausible comparators cover narrower approval, scope, replay, preflight, or UI seams and must remain distinct members or consumers.

No comparator owns synchronization between primary and fallback approval surfaces with single-decision authority and disconnect recovery. Blocked persistence, replay, UX or action-ID contracts are related but distinct.

The reject-all-pending and deny-cascade state machine, including concurrent membership, rollback, and session revocation, is not duplicated. Related approval scope, replay, persistence, and action features address only neighboring slices.

No comparator defines the same multi-surface approval reply mapping, synchronization, replay, timeout, accessibility, and localization seam. The listed features are narrower blocked, UX, or action contracts.

The anchor spans command discovery, template expansion, shell authority, containment, limits, redaction, and MCP compatibility. Comparator features isolate particular include, shell, preview, prompt, package, or global-input concerns; umbrella/member and shared untrusted-input vocabulary do not merge them.

The permission-reply vocabulary-to-transition and error-mapping contract is not replicated. Related comparator features concern persisted approval identity, UX disclosure, domain scoping, or stale action authorization.

No comparator shares the composer-input blocking UI lifecycle, blocker stacking, focus, announcement, reconnect, and stale-recovery outcome. Generic blocked episodes and approval actions are adjacent only.
The anchor is specifically a concept-only login and privacy fixture with no production contract. Docker auth UX and canonical auth or OAuth models have different authorities, states, and outcomes.
No comparator governs the same concept-window destructive Remove affordance. Other visible-action, disable, and setup rollback lifecycles are only structurally analogous.
After comparing all 219 features, none addresses the same custom skill-row interaction targets, roles, accessible names, and repeated skill-surface outcome.

The anchor is a specific masked-key concept fixture excluded from acceptance evidence. Secret-exclusion, reference-first evidence, and redaction-oracle features are plausible neighbors but have different product authority and failure semantics.

This concept settings bundle spans credentials, retention, diagnostics, scope, and permission choices. Comparator features govern distinct evidence, identity, credential, diagnostic, or runtime-context lifecycles, so they are related members rather than equivalents.

No comparator shares the authority and user outcome of tool and project filesystem-scope settings. Path validation, include containment, local writes, FileSafe events, package paths, and cwd invalidation are distinct enforcement or runtime neighbors.

The retrieval-and-search allow, ask, deny surface lacks a resource and policy authority model. Generic approval ceilings, caller-scoped capabilities, domain targets, and durable reuse do not define the same retrieval permission feature.

No comparator governs Assistant Memory's authoritative collection, retention, deletion, and privacy lifecycle. The plan-map routing gap and background runtime-context retention are related but distinct authorities and data sets.
Exhaustive review found no comparator for the unnamed Assistant Memory numeric parameters, their units, bounds, invalid states, and acceptance oracles.

The local blocklist path and command allowlist need one parsing, precedence, refresh, audit, and enforcement contract. Comparator authority-precedence, expansion, profile-ceiling, and decision-policy features remain distinct.

No comparator has the same unwired File Access and Advanced Security settings surface, command identity, state, and enforcement recovery contract. Generic GUI proof, path, FileSafe, and package concerns are adjacent only.

The local Docker executable values are specifically concept fixtures excluded from proof. A generic schema weakness in GUI wiring proof is related but does not share the fixture identity, authority, or outcome.

Docker-versus-Podman runtime selection, executable discovery, precedence, portability, and migration are not duplicated. Docker UI, CLI/API ownership, host matrices, identity, and lifecycle are neighboring but distinct features.

The concept's global rules, per-tool defaults, path patterns, requested/effective state, and enforcement precedence form a distinct access-control surface. Comparator approval and precedence features are upstream or narrower contracts.

No comparator governs the same concept-only Browser Permissions, restart, and recovery controls that require concrete UICommands or retirement. Browser ownership, login, blocked recovery, routes, and action IDs are distinct seams.
All 219 comparators were reviewed; none addresses the semantic identity, range, defaulting, privilege, and validation contract for the bare SSH port value.

No comparator shares the SSH authentication selector's credential source, storage, host-key, fallback, prompt, offline, recovery, and audit boundary. Remote-helper authenticity, path trust, and SSH-secret discovery policy are distinct neighbors.

The anchor is the Permissions System's explicit fail-closed canonical path matching contract. Include paths, overrides, FileSafe events, package paths, and runtime cwd invalidation consume or parallel that policy without sharing its authority and lifecycle.

No comparator duplicates the full layered permission SSOT, downward-only inheritance, specificity, and requested/effective disclosure contract. The listed features are confirmations or consumers of particular precedence and disclosure slices.

The path-object substitution gap concerns canonicalized object identity through open. Include traversal, commit races, approval-target races, generic mutation races, and cwd invalidation have different objects, authorities, and failure outcomes.

The anchor owns approval_scope_key canonical field identity, serialization, normalization, versioning, and equality. Comparator features use, bind, or delegate to that key while governing snapshot, target, domain, reuse, or account semantics, so they are consumers rather than equivalents.

No comparator duplicates PS-119's provider-route type, non-secret locator, proof metadata, snapshot, and redaction custody contract. Secret storage, Docker credentials, leak oracles, provider artifacts, redaction, and executor persistence are adjacent domains.

The contradiction between allowed account/profile references and forbidden account identifiers is unique to the provider-route custody model. Other identity lifecycle, actor envelope, and account-binding features do not resolve that category boundary.

No comparator governs registrable-domain approval broadening across actual host, root host, site, pattern, and domain copy. URL egress, openLink authority, and domain approval dimensions are plausible but distinct.

The contradiction between session approval promotion and narrowing-only resolution is not duplicated. Generic non-widening, child ceiling, and durable reuse contracts are related authority rules with different transitions.
Exhaustive review found no comparator for the malformed normative batch-webfetch field declarations; other web features have different authority, lifecycle, and failure semantics.

The anchor is the generic exact, non-bypassable external-publication guard with chained effect ordering and partial-remote failure semantics. Docker and Decision Policy features are domain members, target-binding rules, or reuse dependencies rather than the same umbrella authority.
No comparator has the same scalar-versus-table collision in the canonical permissions TOML and repeated guard examples; syntactic contradictions in other products are not the same feature.
The missing rule_id in the durable-rule acceptance shape is a specific revocation-key oracle defect. Snapshot replay, approval anchor, and durable reuse lifecycle features are related but distinct.

No comparator owns the contradiction between memory-only session approvals and a persisted merged active-session projection without expiry cleanup. Snapshot lifetime, projection rebuild, restart rehydration, and durable reuse are distinct seams.

The anchor explicitly joins effective permission rows, provenance, and seglog audit outcomes. Identity disclosure, projection events, history rebuild, privacy, and provider propagation are neighboring projection contracts with different authorities.
All comparators were considered; none defines the same conflicting offline versus ask-gated Read-only web preset identifiers, defaults, and selection rules.

The Permissions blocked-outcome addendum owns generic target preflight, in-flight dedupe, revalidation, and indeterminate reconciliation. Container outcomes and Decision Policy or Executor rules are domain applications or prerequisite contracts, not merge-equivalent.

No comparator addresses the closed permission snapshot source enum's inability to encode its own precedence and clamp sources. Other policy, identity, health, availability, and reuse enums govern distinct state models.

The collision among permission blocked-family, recovery-state, reason-code minima, and the later closed blocked_reason_code enum is unique. Host blockers, Docker statuses, health and availability vocabularies, and recovery readiness are analogous but distinct.

No comparator shares the exact approval-resolution transaction ordering among new lineage, frozen snapshot, durable wakeup, idempotency, target revalidation, and blocked-to-runnable scheduling. The listed features each govern only a neighboring identity, replay, preflight, action, or readiness slice.

The anchor concerns product-behavior oracles for the Permissions System's own PlanUnits. Generic GUI evidence, provider evidence, Commands PlanUnits, and Executor PlanUnits have similar validation weakness but different product authorities and behaviors.

The Permissions System anchor defines the actor/lane approval boundary and its complete runtime, blocked-state, remote-effect, provider-gap, GUI, and trust-projection consumer map. Comparator owner splits, blocked contracts, capability gates, domain approvals, and executor action gates are consumers or members rather than the same authority.
